bull.b: Strong revenue, comparable-sales, and traffic growth indicates broad customer demand rather than expansion alone. Sustained visits and sales productivity can support operating leverage, strengthen brand momentum, and provide a durable base for continued restaurant growth over the next several quarters.

High new-unit productivity and rising average unit volumes suggest CAVA can replicate its concept effectively as it expands. With management reiterating 75–77 net new restaurants for 2026, the unit pipeline offers a durable avenue for revenue growth and brand scale.

bull.t: Strong Liquidity and Operating Cash Flow
bull.b: Substantial liquidity and positive operating cash flow give CAVA capacity to fund restaurant openings, absorb operating variability, and support initiatives without immediate financing dependence. This financial flexibility strengthens execution of the expansion plan and improves resilience over the medium term.

bear.b: The sharp reduction from 2024 profitability shows that strong sales growth has not translated consistently into margins. Persistent normalization or cost pressure could limit earnings conversion, reduce operating leverage from new units, and make results more sensitive to execution over coming quarters.

bear.t: Rising Food, Labor, and Delivery Costs
bear.b: Multiple cost categories are increasing simultaneously, including food, wages, and delivery-related operating expenses. These pressures can persist as the company invests in labor and changes food preparation, creating a structural risk that revenue growth will be accompanied by weaker restaurant-level profitability.

Positive operating cash flow is not yet converting fully into discretionary free cash flow because CAVA continues to reinvest heavily. Lower cash conversion can constrain internally funded expansion, reduce capital-allocation flexibility, and leave less financial cushion if operating conditions weaken.
